questions.scenario: A `SavingsAccount` subclass defines its own `__init__` to add an interest rate, but after construction the base `Account` attributes like `balance` are missing.
questions.question: What was forgotten?
options: The base class attributes are inherited automatically with no call needed.
The subclass `__init__` must call `super().__init__(...)` so the base class sets up its own attributes.
questions.explanation: When a subclass defines its own constructor, it overrides the base one, so the base initialization no longer runs unless you call `super().__init__(...)`. That call lets the base class set up `balance` and the rest before the subclass adds its own.
questions.misconception: Defining a subclass `__init__` does not auto-run the parent's. You must call `super().__init__` explicitly.

questions.question: What does method overriding mean?
options: A method accepts a different number of arguments depending on the call.
A subclass provides its own implementation of a method already defined in the base class.
Two methods in the same class share a name.
questions.explanation: Overriding is a subclass redefining an inherited method to change its behavior. Calls on a subclass instance then use the subclass version. Having two same-named methods differing by arguments would be overloading, which Python does not support in the classic sense.

questions.scenario: A class inherits from two parents that both define a method with the same name.
questions.question: How does Python decide which one runs, and what is this called?
options: The method resolution order (MRO) determines it, following C3 linearization left to right through the base classes.
The last-listed parent always wins unconditionally.
Python raises an error on any multiple inheritance.
questions.explanation: Python computes a method resolution order using C3 linearization, a deterministic ordering of the class and its ancestors. A lookup walks that order and uses the first match. This is also how the diamond problem is resolved cleanly.
questions.misconception: Multiple inheritance is not forbidden or random in Python. The MRO gives a well-defined lookup order.
